question: What is area of a rhombus which has diagonals 10 cm and 8 cm?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

Area = (1/2) × 10 × 8

Area = 5 × 8 = 40 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first diagonal (d₁) = 10 cm

Length of second diagonal (d₂) = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rhombus = (Product of diagonals) / 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29c9f2afd18f4d6406144c4d02a912be1a77d17b10fdc321cdad0d0b661d4d0e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (d₁ × d₂) / 2

⇒ Area = (10 × 8) / 2

⇒ Area = 80 / 2

⇒ Area = 40 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Rhombus

The perimeter is calculated as 4 × side. All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length.

Side and Diagonal Relationship

The side of a rhombus can be found using the formula: side = (1/2) × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Diagonal Properties

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).</p
